title: Trigger latency budget bucketing experiment notes
content:
Objective:
Test whether splitting incoming load into small latency-budget buckets reduces noisy scale activity and improves both p95 latency and cost per token for regional GPU pools. Goal is to find a trigger composition that reduces oscillation without adding >5% tail latency or >3% cost overhead vs baseline.

Background / motivation:
- Current min/max autoscaler reacts on aggregated queue pressure and p95 across a heterogeneous set of model groups in a region.
- This causes noisy scale-ups during rapid short spikes and unnecessary scale-downs as pressure drops — leads to cold starts and higher billable GPU-hours.
- Hypothesis: grouping similar workload shapes into latency-budget buckets (short vs long sequences, bursty vs steady) and applying bucket-specific smoothing reduces churn and keeps p95 within SLO while lowering effective reserved capacity.

Experiment design (sheet style):
Columns: bucket_id | description | selection criteria | p95_budget_ms | smoothing_window_min | min_replicas | max_replicas | trigger_metric | trigger_threshold | run_label
Rows:
B1 | short-chat-bursty | qps>20 && median_seq_len<64 | 120ms | 2 | 2 | 40 | p95(service_time) | >120ms sustained 30s | EXP-A
B2 | long-context | median_seq_len>=512 | 500ms | 5 | 1 | 20 | queue_depth_per_replica | >60% sustained 60s | EXP-A
B3 | embed-heavy | embeddings small payloads | 80ms | 1 | 1 | 60 | rps_per_replica | >70% sustained 20s | EXP-B
B4 | background-batch | offline/batched low-priority | 2000ms | 15 | 0 | 10 | scheduled window only | n/a | EXP-C

Trigger variants tested:
- Variant 1 (baseline): global p95 over region triggers scale decisions (current prod-like).
- Variant 2: per-bucket triggers, immediate scale up when bucket p95 > budget, scale-down uses bucket-specific smoothing window (minutes).
- Variant 3: per-bucket plus cross-bucket headroom policy (if adjacent bucket underutilized, allow temporary borrow up to 10% without scaling up).
- Variant 4: per-bucket with exponential backoff on scale-down (longer cool-downs for high-cost models).

Runs and measurements:
Columns: run_label | variant | duration_h | regions | gpu_type | avg_util% | p95_ms(region weighted) | cold_starts_per_hour | scale_ops_per_hour | estimated_extra_gpu_hours | notes
Rows:
EXP-A | Variant 2 | 72 | us-west1, eu-west1 | A100 80GB | 62% | 140ms -> 130ms (improved) | 1.8 -> 0.6 | 12 -> 5 | -18% hours (reduction) | fewer oscillations, B1 smoothing key
EXP-B | Variant 3 | 48 | us-west1 | V100/RTX mixed | 68% | 155ms -> 135ms | 2.6 -> 0.9 | 18 -> 7 | -12% hours | cross-bucket borrow prevented some spikes but complexity higher
EXP-C | Variant 4 | 96 | eu-west1 | A100 80GB | 58% | 150ms -> 148ms | 1.2 -> 0.4 | 9 -> 3 | -21% hours | long cool-down reduced scale-down churn for large models
EXP-BASE | Baseline | 72 | us-west1, eu-west1 | mixed | 70% | 165ms | 3.4 | 20 | baseline | prod-like behavior for comparison

Quick interpretation of numbers:
- All per-bucket variants reduced scale operations/hr by ~50-65% vs baseline.
- p95 improved in most runs (10-18% relative) except in a few long-context edge bursts where tighter budgets caused transient queuing; mitigated by increasing smoothing_window.
- Estimated GPU-hours reduced materially (12-21% in runs) because fewer unnecessary scale-ups + faster scale-down policy tuning.
- Cold starts decreased significantly (factor ~3x reduction in many runs) which improves real user latency experience.

Lessons learned / emergent signals:
- Bucket selection matters more than trigger math: mis-clustered workloads with mixed seq_len+qps still cause cross-noise. Spent ~1 day refining heuristics for selecting buckets from request metadata.
- Small smoothing windows (1-2 min) help bursty short-chat buckets; long-context needs longer smoothing (5-15 min) to avoid thrash.
- Cross-bucket borrowing reduces unnecessary scale-ups for low-cost buckets but adds complexity to accounting and billing. Needs product discussion for charged lines.
- Mixed GPU fleet (different GPU types) revealed that scale decisions must be aware of model->GPU affinity or we get inefficient packing.

Proposed recommended policy (hybrid):
- Implement per-bucket triggers as default, with:
  - short-chat-buckets: p95_budget=120ms, smoothing=2m, min=2, max=40
  - long-context: p95_budget=500ms, smoothing=7m, min=1, max=20
  - embed-heavy: rps budget + 1m smoothing, aggressive scale-out for sustained high rps
- Add a cross-bucket soft-headroom layer that allows temporary borrow (10% of adjacent bucket capacity) without immediate scale-up; limit to 5 minutes.
- Persist bucket assignments and allow manual override per-customer.
- Add affinity-aware packing rule to avoid scaling GPUs of wrong class; prefer same-GPU type scale-up when model pinned.

Operational checklist for rollout (staged):
1) Canary in us-west1 on non-critical accounts for 2 weeks (small % of traffic) - metric: scale_ops/hr, p95, cold_starts, cost delta.
2) Iterate heuristics for bucket selection using 48h of real traffic.
3) Enable cross-bucket borrowing behind feature flag and monitor for unfairness.
4) Full region rollout after 4 weeks if metrics within thresholds.

Telemetry and dashboards to add (sheet/table):
- Per-bucket: p50/p95/p99, avg_replicas, queue_depth, rps_per_replica, scale_ops/hr
- Cross-bucket borrow events: count, duration, effective borrowed_capacity
- Cost dashboard: effective GPU-hours by bucket, cold-start cost estimator

Open questions / risks:
- Billing model: cross-bucket borrowing complicates attribution to customers/teams. Need finance input.
- Edge-case workloads that oscillate across buckets (session length increases mid-session) — how to handle moving sessions?
- Long cold-start models (large-context) still penalize short-chat buckets if incorrectly scheduled; need stronger model->GPU affinity rules.

Action items (owners):
- Diego: prototype bucket assignment service (JIRA-ENG-4891).
- Samir: add per-bucket telemetry to main autoscaler (pull request link above).
- Priya: coordinate finance check on borrowed capacity attribution.
- Aisha (owner): schedule canary, runbook, rollback criteria, and publish experiment write-up to Confluence.

Notes to self / TODOs:
